entries.name: Ronald Satchel

expected.charges: Attempted murder; weapons charges (indicted, later dropped)
expected.sentence:
Shot four times but survived the Dec 4, 1969 police raid on Fred Hampton's apartment. Attempted-murder and weapons indictments against him were dropped after falsified police lab evidence was exposed; he became a plaintiff in the $47.7 million civil-rights suit.

Verdict as recorded: No — attempted-murder and weapons indictments dropped after police lab evidence was shown to be falsified

updates.sentence: Wounded and taken into custody following the December 4, 1969 raid on the Chicago apartment where Fred Hampton and Mark Clark were killed. Released on $25,000 bond December 15, 1969, according to the same-day FBI teletype recording Chicago police information. The later dismissal of the indictments in 1970 was not his custody-release date.

entries.rationale: FBI Chicago December 15, 1969 six-page daily-summary teletype, PDF pp5-7, states Satchel was released that day on $25,000 bond. Replace unsupported 1970 release year tied to charge dismissal; add actual raid custody start.

updates.sentence: Detained after the December 4, 1969 raid and released during December 1969. The December 15 FBI daily summary identifies Deborah Johnson as already out of custody; the exact release day remains unverified. The indictments were dismissed later, in 1970.

entries.rationale: December 15 FBI teletype expressly identifies Deborah Johnson as already out of custody. Combined with December 4 detention this establishes December 1969 release month, not an exact day.
